metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.4) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often over-estimates continuation; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and price is trending up, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 1–4% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently under-estimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 30d.
- If recent 18-day price history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), model tends to over-forecast recovery; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is positive but price is flat or slightly declining, model often over-optimistic; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.
- Model under-responds to official events (e.g., policy changes, emissions targets) when sentiment is neutral; add 1–3% adjustment if event is imminent or confirmed.
